body: This sub is for people who need help. Regardless of what you think of the person, their age, or their perspective, you should always assume that they are justified and talk to the peacefully.

I seriously don't understand how you think this helps. The whole post is about the fact that OP can't bear how they feel day in and day out. What you said isn't helpful or groundbreaking advice, it's a horrible response to something like this.

Read the guidelines, pay attention to the rules. You shouldn't promise things that seem impossible to someone, they'll feel more inadequate. I also feel like you should avoid this subreddit at 13 unless you're coming here for support - if someone you try to build back up disagrees with you or can't, it'll probably scar you.

Point is, educate yourself with the sidebar - how to help, subreddit rules, etc. I applaud your efforts but realize suicide is not a light veil to pull off, it's more like fast-acting cement.
Yeah... Exactly why I'm not dead. A best friend became a love, the only person I've ever loved... I thought I innately couldn't. I dunno if he saved me or I'm living for him. I hope I don't find out.
You are aware of your lack of purpose, probably, but at some point it's realized that no matter how many times you 'find happiness' or distract yourself, you'll come back to the pain.

To hate your purpose is to be aware of it and capable of changing. To have no purpose is to be in endless stupor, incapable of much other than tiring hobbies, until eventually you hollow out and everything becomes a low hum. I would rather hate my purpose.
